questions.question: What is the Bill of Rights, and name five rights it protects?
questions.expected_answer: The Bill of Rights is Chapter 2 of the Constitution, and it lists the rights of everyone in South Africa. Rights include equality, human dignity, life, freedom of religion and expression, peaceful protest, voting for citizens, education, language and culture, a healthy environment, and access to housing, health care, food, water and social security.

questions.question: Explain why rights come with responsibilities, giving three examples.
questions.expected_answer: Rights must not be used to harm the rights of others, so every right comes with duties. With the right to equality comes the responsibility to treat others equally and not discriminate. With the right to education comes the responsibility to attend school, work hard and not disrupt others. With the right to a healthy environment comes the responsibility not to litter or pollute. With freedom of expression comes the responsibility not to spread lies or hate.

questions.question: Describe the life and work of Pius Langa.
questions.expected_answer: Pius Langa was born in 1939 in Bushbuckridge and later lived and worked in KwaZulu-Natal. He left school early, worked in a factory and finished school by private study. He worked in the Department of Justice as an interpreter and messenger while studying law part-time through the University of South Africa. He became an advocate in Durban in 1977 and defended activists and people treated unfairly under apartheid. In 1994, Mandela appointed him to the first Constitutional Court, and he was Chief Justice from 2005 to 2009. He died in 2013.
